author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Kim Ahern won the Democratic nomination for Rhode Island attorney general Wednesday, emerging from a four-candidate primary with about 36% of the vote in unofficial results reported by NBC 10.

Ahern previously chaired the state Cannabis Control Commission and served as a special assistant attorney general under three Rhode Island attorneys general. She defeated Keith Hoffmann, state Rep. Joe Solomon Jr. and state Rep. Jason Knight. Hoffmann had the endorsement of incumbent Attorney General Peter Neronha.

The office is open because Neronha is barred by term limits from seeking reelection. The primary placed experience inside the attorney general’s office, legislative backgrounds and competing enforcement priorities before Democratic voters.

Ahern used her victory remarks to emphasize public safety, access to health care, environmental protection, energy costs, affordability and the principle that government officials must remain accountable to the law. The result is unofficial until the state completes its canvass and certification process. Ahern now advances to the November general election, when voters will decide who succeeds Neronha as Rhode Island’s chief legal officer.
dek: The former Cannabis Control Commission chair emerged from a four-candidate field with about 36% of the unofficial vote.
headline: Kim Ahern wins Rhode Island Democratic attorney general primary
